Toys & Collectibles Lego "So f****** peak" - Fan who made incredible Lego GTA 6 set is at it again with the perfect PlayStation diorama News By Benjamin Abbott Published 12 October 2026 Upgrading the console into the ultimate Final Fantasy 7 diorama When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here's how it works . (Image credit: Iain Wilson) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A fan has taken it upon themselves to upgrade the new Lego PlayStation set, and dear reader, my jaw was dropped. Prolific builder hachiroku24 (who you may know for their phenomenal Lego GTA 6 set ) has made a genuinely impressive Final Fantasy 7 diorama via reddit with 4K upvotes that sits on top of the Lego PlayStation, which just came out at the Lego store . It features most major characters in a life-or-death battle and is beautifully well-done; pieces of terrain are growing out of the console as if the action can't be contained on a disc, and some minifigures are actually using the controller as a springboard to launch their next attack. As noted in our five-star Lego PlayStation review , this is already a brilliant model... but the FF7 overlay makes it even better. As mentioned in a top comment on the reddit thread, "it's so fucking peak." Latest Videos From GamesRadar+ Watch full video here: I made a Final Fantasy VII diorama using the Playstation 1 as a base from r/lego This isn't the first time hachiroku24 has made a kick-ass Final Fantasy 7 model; they submitted a Midgar diorama to the Ideas program, and I really hope it becomes a real set . Because these designs can reach the desk of Lego itself if they get enough fan-votes (as will happen with the new Lego Marvel and Star Wars crossover ), there's a chance we may see their work on a shelf one day. Considering how consistently they keep knocking it out of the park, I've got my fingers crossed. Unfortunately, there's no word on how to build this for ourselves, but it all starts with making the PlayStation from the Lego store and then finding the right pieces to create your own slice of Midgar - and you can get whatever you need from Lego's Pick a Brick service .
